newsitem.title: USA: Baxter earnings up, sales hurt by currency exchanges.
newsitem.headline: Baxter earnings up, sales hurt by currency exchanges.

text.p: Baxter International Inc. Thursday reported strong fourth-quarter results that industry analysts said provided the first clear view of the healthcare products giant since its latest restructuring.

The company said, however, that the stronger dollar reduced its sales by about $30 million in the fourth quarter and $108 million for the year. Non-U.S. sales comprise more than half of the Deerfield, Ill.-based company's total revenues.
The company's stock jumped $3.625 to $46 on the New York Stock Exchange as investors applauded the results and Baxter's outlook for 1997.

"Investors are obviously encouraged that the company's top-line growth has shown a strong upturn following a sluggish performance in the third quarter," said Bear Stearns healthcare industry analyst Frederick Wise.

Baxter reported fourth-quarter operating profits of $158 million, or 58 cents per share, up from $148 million, or 54 cents a share, a year ago. The results were 1 cent per share ahead of Wall Street estimates compiled by First Call.
Baxter's businesses include biotechnology, cardiovascular medicine, products and services for kidney disease, and intravenous systems and products.

The company's quarterly sales of $1.49 billion were up 10 percent from $1.34 billion a year ago. That growth rate would have been 12 percent without the effect of the stronger dollar, said Baxter Chief Financial Officer Harry Kraemer.
Baxter last fall spun off its hospital supplies and cost management services units into a new company, Allegiance Corp., which is based in McGaw Park, Ill.

"We've had three or four quarters that have had extremely confusing results because of the spin-off. This is the first quarter where the numbers were clearly positive in every aspect of the business," Wise said.
Sales for all of 1996 were $5.44 billion, up 8 percent from $5.05 billion. Without currency translations, that growth rate would have been 10 percent.
"Even though our sales came in $108 million less, we hit our earnings commitment," Kraemer said of the year's results.

After closing its $623 million acquisition of Switzerland's Immuno International AG in mid-1997, Baxter said it expects as much as 60 percent of sales and 75 percent of profits to come from outside the United States.
Kraemer said the company expects revenues to be near $6.5 billion this year.
For the year Baxter's operating earnings rose to $575 million, or $2.11 a share, from $371 million, or $1.34 a share, a year earlier.
